evidence: Here Come the Lords (Pendulum and Elektra, 1993) credits Marley Marl with sole or shared production on every track and with mixing all of them, frequently with K-Def. 'Funky Child' was produced by Marl and K-Def at Marl's House of Hits. A track on the album samples Marl's own 1985 record 'Marley Marl Scratch'.

later.title: Lord Jazz Hit Me One Time (Make It Funky)

trackPair.whatToListenFor: Here the producer samples himself. 'Marley Marl Scratch' is one of his first records, from before sampling drums was his method. Eight years later a piece of it turns up inside a Lords of the Underground track he produced. Listen for the older record returning as material, and for how it's become a sound source inside a bigger, busier 1993 production built around the group's DJ.

explanation.age7: Marley Marl made beats for Lords of the Underground, and even used a piece of one of his own old songs.
explanation.age13: Lords of the Underground recorded their first album at Marley Marl's studio. He produced or co-produced every song, often with his student K-Def. On one track they used a piece of a record Marl made back in 1985, so his old music became part of the new.
explanation.adult: The edge shows the producer's lineage continuing (Marl to K-Def) and the producer's own catalogue becoming sample material. The last is a small, clear case of the self-referencing that sampling made possible.
